//: DD32. The line that makes DockerDesk's read/do split pay. Nothing installs this for you:
an allowlist is where a tool editing your configuration without asking would be least
forgivable, so the install ships the line and you decide.
Merge the `allow` entry into your own .claude/settings.json — per project, or into
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json for every project on this machine. If you already
have a permissions.allow array, add the one string to it rather than replacing the file.
`read` is a promise and not a prefix: every verb under it is handed a handle with no start,
no remove and no prune on it, and a test drives every registered read verb and requires
every request it made to be a GET. That is what makes one line safe to grant.
`do` is deliberately absent. Starting an engine or removing what a session created is worth
an approval, and granting it here would undo the reason the split exists.
